prompt:
Image 1 is the pose and layout guide: four grey clay maquettes of this creature in a 2 by 2 grid, one action in each cell, rendered from the game's battle camera. Copy from it exactly, cell by cell, the camera angle, the direction the body faces, the pose, the figure's size and its place in the cell. Do not copy its smooth clay surfaces, its simplified round shapes or the thickness of its limbs: the body, its anatomy and every detail follow Image 2.
Image 2 is the approved painted game cutout of this exact creature, standing at rest, seen from the same camera in the same view. Paint the same individual, with exactly the same head, shapes, proportions, colours, materials, markings and equipment, in the same painting style and the same light, now in the actions of Image 1. It must be unmistakably the same creature in all four cells.

One sheet: four painted figures of the same creature, full body, one in each cell of a 2 by 2 grid, on a perfectly flat, uniform pure blue (#0000FF) background, as game cutouts. Read left to right, top row first:
Top left: struck in the air: the body thrown back, the wings flared out unevenly, the head jerked back.
Top right: diving to attack: the wings swept back close to the body, the head and beak pointing forward and down, the tail streaming behind.
Bottom left: burnt out and falling: the wings collapsing and folding, the head drooping, the body tumbling out of the air (the game adds the embers; paint none).
Bottom right: dead: lying crumpled on the ground, the wings spread limp over the ground, the head on the ground, the plumage darker, charred (no embers, no fire).
Every cell takes its pose from Image 1, never from Image 2: Image 2 shows only what the creature looks like, and its standing pose must not be copied into any cell. Each pose is strong and unmistakable at a glance.

Camera: high above and behind, looking down at about 40 degrees, the way a player looks down at a miniature on a table; orthographic, with no perspective. The creature faces away from us, toward the upper right of the image, as in Image 1 and Image 2: we see its back, its right side and the top of its head from behind; its face is hidden. It is foreshortened as seen from above: the top of the head, the shoulders or back and the upper body are large, the legs short.

Light: outdoor daylight, exactly as in Image 2; the figure stays as dark and as muted as in Image 2, lit only by small warm and cool highlights, never washed out or brightened. A high sun in the upper left of the image lights the top and the upper-left side with warm highlights; a cool blue-grey sky fill lies in the shadows on the lower-right side. No candlelight, no dramatic dark shadows. Nothing glows more than it does in Image 2. No cast shadow on the background.

Painting style: painterly oil on a wood panel, visible directional brushwork, moderate detail, exactly the hand of Image 2; a muted earthy palette with its own colours exactly as Image 2 shows them; soft painterly edges, small crisp highlights and a thin bright rim of light along the upper-left edges. A strong, simple, readable silhouette in every pose. It is not a cartoon: no cel shading, no thick black outlines, no chibi or big-headed proportions, no glossy 3D render, no pixel art.

The god: the Ash Phoenix, an undying firebird-god of ash and ember that rises again after death. Colours: muted and earthy. The one clear colour of the bird is its long flight feathers: dull ember-orange (#C4532C), the Cinder Horde's colour. All metal is dull old gold (#C9A23E), darkened and worn. Nothing in the image glows: there is no flame, no fire and no glow. No other saturated area larger than a small clasp or trim.
Body: a great bird of prey shaped like an eagle with a long neck; its body feathers are coal-dark, charred black-brown (#3A2A24), each barred with thin pale ash-grey bars; a hooked beak of dull old gold (#C9A23E), darkened and worn; dark eyes; strong taloned feet of dark grey. Crest: a tall plume crest of long feathers sweeping back from its brow. Wings: broad, rounded wings spread like fans, the long flight feathers dull ember-orange (#C4532C), the Cinder Horde's colour, barred with darker bands. Tail: a long tail of trailing feathers.
There is no flame, no glow and no trail of embers: the game draws them.

Size: in each cell the figure fills the cell exactly as its maquette does in Image 1 and stands in the same place, with clean background all round it; nothing is cropped and no part of one figure reaches into a neighbouring cell.

Background: one flat pure blue (#0000FF) colour fills the whole image with no gradient, texture, floor, vignette or shadow. No blue, cyan or violet anywhere on the figure.

Never: text, letters, numbers, labels, grid lines, dividing lines between the cells, borders, frames, signatures, logos; a floor, ground, scenery or cast shadows; blood; other creatures or people; a cropped figure; fire, flames, breath, smoke, sparks, floating embers, magic light or mist (the game draws every effect).
